findings.title: Ruined dwellings preserve stillness as testimony
findings.reading: The word `مَسَٰكِنِهِمْ` is a plural possessed dwelling noun, and its root field includes settling, repose, and stillness alongside habitation. In the ruin setting, the ordinary dwelling sense remains the anchor, but the places that once held a settled population now survive as still witnesses. The Form V disclosure wording lets those settled sites become legible testimony, while the settlement-reversal model makes the interpretive change explicit: the instruments of permanence expose the failure of permanence. This is a controlled lexical overlap between dwelling and stillness, not permission to replace the noun with an unrelated root gloss.

findings.title: The base parse makes dwellings the governed source
findings.reading: In `مِّن مَّسَٰكِنِهِمْ`, the base morphology makes `مَسَٰكِنِهِمْ` genitive under the source preposition `مِنْ`. The local construction therefore presents the dwellings as the origin or source from which clarity is obtained. A supplied variant can give the dwellings stronger nominative agency as clarifiers, but that variant is a contrastive pressure on the base parse, not a replacement for it. The reading changes the scene from dwellings merely being mentioned near an insight to dwellings governing the evidential route.

findings.title: The source preposition turns place into an evidence channel
findings.reading: The preposition `مِنْ` attaches the dwelling phrase to the clarity verb as a source or medium: the evidence comes from the settled remains. Attachment evidence strongly favors this source relation, yet the supplied ambiguity permits a secondary pressure in which the peoples are identified through their remains. That pressure remains controlled by the local syntax. The interpretive gain is a double visibility of place as both the material source of disclosure and the identifying trace of the people who once occupied it.

findings.title: The opening conjunction carries an inherited frame
findings.reading: The initial `وَ` before `عَادًا` is coordinating a carried accusative name sequence rather than beginning an isolated sentence. Its attachment evidence preserves continuation from an already-running destruction frame. The ayah therefore opens mid-stream: the named peoples arrive already under inherited governance, and the reader is made to carry the preceding frame into the new evidence and diversion clauses.

findings.title: Certified disclosure interrupts and addresses the reader
findings.reading: The conjunction before `قَدْ` opens a parenthetical evidence span and shifts the discourse from the third-person peoples to the second-person audience in `لَكُمْ`. `قَدْ` certifies the following perfect `تَبَيَّنَ` as already established. The Form V verb can then be heard as clarity emerging from the evidence itself, with the dwellings as its source, while the dative audience becomes witness to what has been made manifest. The wording changes the relation to the ruins: the passage does not only report an ancient failure; it directs an already-verified disclosure toward the hearers. The self-manifesting reading remains a lexical and syntactic possibility, not a claim that no other agency can ever explain the clarity.

findings.title: A resumptive conjunction returns to the causal story
findings.reading: After the evidence parenthesis, the conjunction before `زَيَّنَ` is a local reconnection point. Attachment evidence separates the disclosure aside from the following main verbal clause, so the conjunction resumes the causal narration without erasing what the aside established. The reading keeps the sequence continuous: visible evidence is inserted, then the account returns to the mechanism by which the peoples were redirected.

findings.title: The second conjunction locks the two names together
findings.reading: The second `وَ`, before `ثَمُودَا۟`, coordinates the two proper names under the same carried syntactic frame. It does more than add another example: it makes ʿAd and Thamud a compact doublet that remains jointly governed as the narration moves into disclosure and diversion. The pair is therefore heard as one named field of peoples under the inherited destruction frame, while each name retains its own formal behavior.

findings.title: Beautification exposes agent, affected group, and object
findings.reading: The Form II active verb `زَيَّنَ` has a visible three-part valency: the definite nominative `ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ` is the agent, `لَهُمُ` marks the group for whom the beautification is routed, and `أَعْمَالَهُمْ` is the direct object. The lām looks benefactive in form but becomes harmful in consequence, producing the supplied irony that what is made attractive for them works against them. The plural suffix is then traceable across the phrase: the same group owns the dwellings, receives the beautification, owns the deeds, and becomes the object of diversion. The grammar keeps agency and affectedness visible instead of hiding them in an impersonal account.

findings.title: Their collected actions become the hinge of diversion
findings.reading: `أَعْمَالَهُمْ` is an accusative plural construct: the collected deeds or practices of the named group are the direct object of `زَيَّنَ`. The root field for action is morally broad, so the noun is not intrinsically wicked; the danger comes from the beautifying operation and the clause that follows it. The word order places the deeds before the causal result, making them the hinge: their purposive activity is made attractive, then becomes the medium through which movement is redirected. This preserves the distinction between action itself and distorted evaluation of action.

findings.title: Fa makes obstruction the immediate consequence
findings.reading: The `فَ` before `صَدَّهُمْ` is a causal-sequential hinge. Attachment evidence identifies the obstruction clause as the result of the beautification clause, so diversion is not an unrelated second fact. The interpretive change is temporal and causal: attractive presentation is followed immediately by turning away, making the decorated appearance part of the mechanism that produces the obstruction.

findings.title: A named adversary carries remoteness into the path break
findings.reading: `ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ` is a definite nominative subject of the beautifying verb, so the mechanism has a named grammatical agent. The remoteness and estrangement branch of the root fits the later `عَنِ` separation from the recognized path, while the rebellious-agent branch supplies the lexical image of an overstepping adversary. The alternative fire derivation remains background only. The reading therefore joins explicit agency with the result of distance: the named agent makes deeds attractive and the people remote from the course, rather than leaving the blockage anonymous.

findings.title: The recognized way remains while access is blocked
findings.reading: In `صَدَّهُمْ`, the attached plural suffix is the direct object of a completed transitive turning-away. The perfect form marks an accomplished obstruction, but it does not erase the object of the following separation frame. `عَنِ` governs the definite singular genitive `ٱلسَّبِيلِ`, making the recognized way the exact target from which they are diverted. The path root keeps its ordinary course or traversable-way sense, with a qualified flow-pressure image that sharpens interference rather than replacing the noun. The changed reading is therefore blocked access: the way still exists, while the people are turned away from it.

findings.title: The closing state makes diversion paradoxical
findings.reading: The final `وَ` coordinates the closing clause but is locally licensed as concessive: the insight-state is attached to the obstruction rather than detached from it. `كَانُوا` is a third-person plural perfect auxiliary, and its following accusative active participle `مُسْتَبْصِرِينَ` states an already-held condition. The plural subject keeps the two named peoples active as one doublet, and the participle classifies both together by a shared perceptual state. The result is a sharper paradox than momentary seeing: they were in a state described as perceptive or discerning, yet that state did not prevent diversion. The root's inner-insight branch is available here; the bodily-sight branch is not silently substituted.

findings.title: Bodily collapse is set against qualified insight
findings.reading: The supplied boundary evidence places the closing participle beside an earlier bodily-collapse image, creating a body-versus-mind contrast: visible ruin and fallen bodies do not imply absent perception. Form X in `مُسْتَبْصِرِينَ` heightens the field of discernment, but the evidence also allows seeking, possessing, or claiming insight, so the reading must not force maximal certainty. What changes is the failure diagnosis: the scene can hold cognitive capacity or a claim to insight together with conduct that still does not follow the recognized path.

findings.title: The ending closes a clarity-available failure envelope
findings.reading: The closing insight participle is linked by its row family to the opening `تَبَيَّنَ` clarity wording and to the concessive final clause. The evidence has already been certified as manifest to the audience, and the peoples are then described in a heightened perceptual state; the envelope closes precisely where perception fails to govern action. This does not claim that every shade of the root is active at once. It preserves the specific connection between established external disclosure, qualified inner insight, and the completed diversion.

findings.title: The paired names keep different case surfaces
findings.reading: `عَادًا` carries accusative tanwin and is treated as a carried object under a recovered governing frame. Its pairing with `ثَمُودَ` is syntactically shared, but the base form of Thamud remains diptotic and therefore does not take the same tanwin. The supplied leveling variant shows that a different surface was possible, making the received asymmetry a live formal pressure rather than a necessary change in objecthood. Case thus keeps the compact name-pair together while allowing the two names to sound different.

findings.title: A return-root echo colors the ʿAd name cautiously
findings.reading: The local item `عَادًا` remains a proper name, so the `ع و د` field of return and recurrence cannot replace its referential function with a free verb meaning. It can, however, create a restrained irony: a name carrying return pressure appears in a ruin scene marked by failed return to the recognized way. The connection is background coloring only, with the name's case and paired-object role kept primary.

findings.title: The Thamud name carries a faint depletion image
findings.reading: `ثَمُودَ` is locally a proper name in the same carried accusative sequence. The supplied root field permits a cautious exhausted-water or depletion image beside the visible remains, but the evidence explicitly narrows that pressure to background coloring. The reading therefore adds a resource-exhaustion echo to the ruin scene without turning the name into an ordinary lexical noun or displacing its proper-name role.

findings.title: Available evidence and insight still fail to govern movement
findings.reading: The qualified focus-local synthesis assembles `تَبَيَّنَ` B004 as emergence and disclosure, `مَسَٰكِنِهِمْ` B002 as settled sites, and `مُسْتَبْصِرِينَ` B002 as inward discernment. Their connection is specific: outward evidence is available from the remains and inner perception is also described, yet the peoples are still diverted. The interpretive change is from a simple failure to see toward a failure of discernment to govern conduct. The nomination is legacy-unbound, so this is a qualified assembled mechanism rather than an independent wider-context proof.

findings.title: Attractive revaluation reroutes active agency
findings.reading: The qualified valuation model links beautifying display (zyn B002), the overstepping adversarial agent (shṭn B004), intentional work (ʿml B001), turning away (ṣdd B001), and the traversed way (sbl B001). The sequence matters: their own purposive deeds remain active, but attractive presentation captures their evaluation of those deeds and reroutes agency toward diversion. This focus-local reading changes the image from an external tempter simply hiding an unseen road to an action-loop in which valuation mediates movement. The source's legacy status is kept visible, and the lexical branches are treated as qualified contacts rather than a forced single root meaning.

findings.title: The settled place reverses into testimony
findings.reading: The settlement-reversal nomination connects `س ك ن` B001, the cessation of motion, with B009, a settled place, and `ب ي ن` B004, becoming manifest. A dwelling normally stabilizes life by giving it a place to remain; here the settled sites outlast their inhabitants only as visible evidence against their claim to durable stability. This mechanism is distinct from the broader evidence-insight gap because it focuses on the reversal of settlement itself. It remains a qualified focus-local model supplied with legacy provenance.

findings.title: Adorned works place a barrier between evidence and way
findings.reading: The supplied published finding joins four concrete contacts: the dwellings become visible evidence through `ب ي ن` B004, inner discernment remains available through `ب ص ر` B002, beautification alters the presentation of deeds through `ز ي ن` B002, and turning away can be heard as a blocking barrier through `ص د د` B001/B005. The resulting reading is that evaluative adornment occupies the space between what can be known and the path that should be followed. The source is a citable cross-run synthesis, but the explanation stays within the assembled focus-local mechanisms and does not import an unstated wider scene.

findings.title: Decorated sight can become a blockage
findings.reading: The focus-local reader activation assembles `ص د د` B001, turning aside, with B005, a blocking mountain image. The dwellings make the outcome visible, while beautified deeds are inferred to form an intervening obstruction between perception and path; the closing perceptive state then intensifies the warning because capacity to see can coexist with a constructed blockage. The packet directly supplies the lexical sequence and the obstruction frame; the mental redirection is an inference and is therefore kept explicitly qualified.

findings.title: Adorned work captures valuation before the turn
findings.reading: The second focus-local reader activation links `زَيَّنَ` B002, `ٱلشَّيْطَانُ` through the supplied opposition/crookedness branch B003, `أَعْمَالَهُمْ` B001, `فَصَدَّهُمْ` B001, and `ٱلسَّبِيلِ` B001. The explicit fa places beautification before diversion, while the retained insight state keeps the mechanism centered on valuation rather than missing information. The proposed attractive self-appraisal that mediates the turn is abductive: the packet supplies the sequence and lexical roles but not a direct mental arrow, so this boundary remains visible.
